diagnosis_explanation: Your brain was injured from an accident. This injury can cause problems with thinking or feeling. It can also affect how you move. Your neck muscles were also strained. This can cause pain and stiffness in your neck.
medication_rationale: Your doctor did not give you any new medicines to take at home. Ask at your next visit if you need to start any.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will likely feel tired and sore. This is normal.
- Rest often. Gentle movement is good for healing.
- Focus on basic self-care activities like washing your face.
- You may have some trouble remembering things. This will get better.
- Your goal is to follow your home exercise plan daily.
- Call your doctor if you have a severe headache or feel very dizzy.

**Week 2:**
- Your energy may start to slowly return.
- Try to increase your walking distance a little each day.
- Practice skills like dressing yourself.
- Focus on simple tasks and avoid getting overwhelmed.
- Your goal is to walk around your home for 10 minutes twice a day.
- Call your doctor if you have new or worsening neck pain.

**Week 3:**
- You might feel a bit stronger and more comfortable.
- You can try doing light chores around the house.
- Keep practicing memory games or doing puzzles.
- Work on improving your balance and coordination.
- Your goal is to walk for 15 minutes without stopping.
- Call your doctor if you experience uncontrolled shaking.

**Week 4:**
- You should notice more energy and less soreness.
- You can try slightly more challenging exercises from your plan.
- Try to return to normal daily routines as you can.
- Focus on regaining your normal coordination.
- Your goal is to walk outside for 20 minutes daily.
- Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing or feel confused.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Healing takes time, so be patient with yourself.
- Keep doing your home exercises every day.
- Continue practicing self-care and memory tasks.
- You will gradually regain your strength and coordination.
- Follow your doctor's advice for the best recovery.
